title: Readiness, process, and cgroup/netns lifecycle integration tests
commit_message: test(lifecycle): verify readiness and resource lifecycle

commands.detail: workspace-level target (plan QA form) resolves in microvm-service and passes
privileged test compiles and prints 'blocked: guest_health_port_unset'; passes without mocking

verification.package_note: The task's run line names '-p microvm-lifecycle', but VmLifecycleService is defined in microvm-service (which depends on microvm-lifecycle). A service-level integration test cannot live in microvm-lifecycle without a dependency cycle, and microvm-lifecycle has no phase/cleanup/supervision concepts. Cargo confirms: 'no test target named lifecycle_cleanup in microvm-lifecycle; help: available test in microvm-service package'. The plan's own QA scenario uses the workspace form 'cargo test --features privileged --test lifecycle_cleanup', which resolves in microvm-service.

acceptance_criteria.success_records_all_phase_timestamps: successful_boot_records_all_phase_timestamps asserts spawn/socket_ready/configured/guest_ready are timestamped and monotonic on boot, and stopped is timestamped (>= guest_ready) on stop
acceptance_criteria.failed_readiness_is_guest_not_ready: vm_is_not_running_until_guest_ready asserts the failure is classified by is_guest_not_ready with err.context[phase]==guest_ready, the VM reconciles to Failed (never Running), guest_ready/stopped phases are never recorded, and the readiness probe was genuinely consulted after exactly one InstanceStart
acceptance_criteria.supervisor_termination_leaves_nothing: supervisor_death_cleans_all_owned_resources_in_order asserts a dead supervisor reconciles the VM to Failed and issues teardown in strict reverse-creation order kill:1000 -> nft -> tap -> netns, with the socket and cgroup leaf removed; normal_stop_releases_every_per_vm_resource and failed_readiness_cleans_up_provisioned_resources assert the socket, cgroup leaf, and netns mount point are gone after stop and after a failed boot
acceptance_criteria.evidence_class_is_privileged: this artifact sets class=privileged, embeds a real host_preflight block, and records the privileged run as blocked (pass=false) on a host lacking pinned firecracker/jailer binaries — never a mock pass
acceptance_criteria.deterministic: readiness gating, process supervision, and cleanup ordering are exercised deterministically via VmLifecycleService over a scripted FirecrackerBackend (no KVM/root/binary, no QEMU TCG, no mock-as-KVM)
acceptance_criteria.privileged_test: privileged::service_boot_guest_ready_stop_cleans_all_resources boots a real Firecracker/jailer through the service and verifies no process/cgroup/TAP/netns/socket remains after stop; it reports a stable blocked token on an incapable host

deliverables.lifecycle_cleanup_suite: crates/microvm-service/tests/lifecycle_cleanup.rs — 7 deterministic integration tests + 1 privileged test, reusing the shared scripted Rig (tests/common/mod.rs) that wires VmLifecycleService over a fully scripted FirecrackerBackend
deliverables.privileged_feature: microvm-service gains a 'privileged' feature that enables microvm-firecracker/privileged and microvm-isolation/privileged, gating the real-Firecracker lane out of the default deterministic run

guardrails.no_mock_as_kvm: the privileged lane follows pass/blocked/failed; on this host (KVM API 12 + TUN + cgroup-v2 present, but firecracker/jailer binaries and boot artifacts absent) it prints 'blocked: guest_health_port_unset' and passes rather than substituting QEMU TCG or a mock for a KVM/Firecracker pass
guardrails.anti_mock_schema_rule: host_preflight.kvm_ok=true here, but the privileged run records pass=false/blocked=true, so the fail-closed anti-mock rule (no pass=true without a real substrate run) is respected
guardrails.readiness_not_process_readiness: Running is asserted only after the guest_ready phase timestamp is recorded; socket_ready alone never advances the VM to Running
guardrails.fail_closed_cleanup: a failed boot (guest not ready) tears down everything provisioned before the gate; a dead supervisor triggers ordered reverse-creation teardown; reconciliation is idempotent and a stopped VM is never spuriously re-torn-down

design_notes.placement: VmLifecycleService composes microvm-lifecycle (state/policy), microvm-firecracker (runtime + phase timestamps), and microvm-isolation (cleanup). The integration test therefore lives in microvm-service, the only crate that can reference the composed service without a dependency cycle.
design_notes.two_cleanup_paths: normal stop uses the backend teardown (graceful wait_exit, then CleanupManager + net.teardown_netns + cgroup.teardown_leaf, removing socket/cgroup/netns filesystem artifacts); supervisor-death reconciliation uses the IsolationCleanup bridge (CleanupManager with the dead supervisor pid, issuing kill -> nft -> tap -> netns through the cleanup backend). The deterministic RecordingCleanupBackend records the privileged teardown commands; the filesystem-owned resources (socket, cgroup leaf, netns mount point) are asserted directly.
design_notes.nft_naming: the backend teardown derives the nft table via ResourceRecord::default_nft_table (dash-folded), while the isolation reconciliation path uses the raw 'microvm_<vm-id>'; the test computes each expected name accordingly.
